programme.title: Alaskan armoilla
programme.desc: This eye-opening series follows the drama and hardships experienced by four Alaskan households in different corners of this merciless territory as they battle to make it through a long, dark, freezing winter. The huge US state of Alaska boasts some of the world's most deadly weather, with temperatures regularly plummeting to a lethal -80 Fahrenheit, freezing exposed limbs in minutes. Yet it is also home to some of the toughest, most resilient, most isolated people in the world. Life is all about survival in the face of unrelenting weather, scarce resources and man-eating carnivores.

She is a no-nonsense personality and refuses to cook Ben any dinner. But as the week progresses she warms to her guest and explains what drew her to the harsh Australian wilderness 30 years ago. She also talks about her complex relationship with men, and reveals how she has been seriously threatened when defending the natural world around her from development.

programme.title: Expedition Killer Whale
programme.desc: In Antarctica, the most sophisticated hunting behaviour in the animal kingdom takes place - killer whales creating waves to wash seals off pieces of floating ice. A team of scientists and filmmakers travel to these freezing waters to find out more about these unique animals and how they do it. And one of the scientists is looking for one killer whale in particular. But their mission is not just to deepen our understanding of this extraordinary hunting behaviour. The team are also intent on learning more about the secret - and more tender side - of the lives of these killer whales.

programme.desc: Ben spends time with 'Pirate' Rob, who he previously met in Slab City, California. Rob lives for half the year with his 18-year-old son Damien in a sandbag house on an island in the middle of the Oregon river. Rob is a doting father who migrates according to the weather and resources. Ben joins him fishing for crayfish, kayaking the school run, and digging a toilet. Pictures.

programme.title: Ben Fogle: Paluu villiin
programme.desc: As one of the world's most in-demand sporting coaches, 43-year-old Nikola Boric once travelled the world, welcomed everywhere he went. Now, he lives in a wooden cabin without electricity, water or heating, with just some pigs and goats for company.

programme.title: Alaskan armoilla
programme.desc: Chip and Agnes are ready to embark on an autumn moose hunt. For Sue, the approaching winter means that she has only a few days to make sure her camp and business are completely closed. In Eagle, early snowfall has left Andy and Kate concerned that winter will come sooner rather than later. Andy decides it's time to hit a nearby pond to see if he can catch a beaver.

programme.title: Alaskan armoilla
programme.desc: Andy discovers the river isn't going to freeze solid in front of his homestead. He must cut a trail through dense forest to cross the river safely and get to his hunting grounds. Sue needs 4,000 gallons of fuel delivered to see her through to next spring, and a storm is threatening to hit before deliveries can get in. Erik needs his bad trapping season to turn around.

programme.title: Changing Planet: River Restoration
programme.desc: Two world-leading projects designed to tackle the crises facing Earth’s rivers come under the spotlight. One in the American West, the other in Paris.

programme.title: Junamatka Eurooppaan
programme.desc: Michael Portillo travels east through the Balkans along the most exotic section of the Orient Express. His destination is Istanbul, a multi-ethnic city where Europe and Asia meet via an underground railway. 1/6.

programme.title: David Attenborough's Natural Curiosities
programme.desc: Sir David Attenborough examines the mysteries behind some of nature's most fascinating creatures and plants. The mystery of where some animals disappear to each year puzzled early naturalists. Do swallows hibernate in mud or under water? Where do butterflies suddenly appear from each spring? The discovery of the swallow's epic migration and the butterfly's magical transformation were scientific stories cloaked in mystery and controversy.

programme.title: Fishing Impossible
programme.desc: Endure a bone-shaking 500-km drive across Kenya as Jay, Blowfish, and Charlie search for Africa’s largest freshwater fish. Brave the croc-infested waters of Lake Turkana, hook a high-altitude trout, and snatch catfish from under the noses of hippos.

programme.title: Pompeii's Secret Underworld
programme.desc: Once thought of as a symbol of Roman sophistication, recent archaeological discoveries at Pompeii uncover a complex and dark reality that was key to the city functioning.

programme.title: Alaskan armoilla
programme.desc: As the frozen landscape of the Arctic melts away, the Alaskans get to work. They take advantage by heading out to hunt and securing their camps to protect them from flooding.

programme.title: Ben Fogle: Paluu villiin
programme.desc: In Tuscany, Ben meets British couple George and Sophie who have breathed new life into a farmhouse. George's desire to live self-sufficiently lead to a lifelong project.

programme.title: Junamatka Eurooppaan
programme.desc: Armed with his 1913 railway guide, Michael Portillo travels the Habsburg imperial line from Vienna across the Semmering Pass, a handmade railway line blasted through the Alps. His destination is the Adriatic port of Trieste. In Vienna, he encounters a pre-Cold War spy and hears about a concert that caused a riot in 1913. At the winter sports resort of Semmering, rails of a slippier kind prove hard to navigate when Michael takes to a toboggan. In Austria's second city, Graz, Michael ventures underground at the Lurgrotte Caves to find out about a famous turn-of-the-century rescue operation. Over the border in the former imperial territory of Slovenia, Michael discovers how an earthquake in Ljubljana encouraged its citizens to assert their national identity in architecture and art. In high spirits, Michael says 'na zdravje' to Slovenia and heads south. Arriving in Italy at the empire's southern port of Trieste, Michael savours the imported coffee which fuelled the cafe culture of Vienna.

programme.title: Wild France
programme.desc: The Atlantic winds blow on a country blessed by nature. A country where the rich, fertile soil has given birth to an exceptional wildlife.

programme.title: Alaskan armoilla
programme.desc: As winter approaches, Denise and Andy scout the river for a large animal to harvest for protein. Sue moves her chicken coop, and Jessie races to finish his project.

programme.title: Ben Fogle: Paluu villiin
programme.desc: Ben meets a photographer living out his childhood dream. Dan Price gave up his job as a photographer to live the remotest of lifestyles in a meadow in Oregon, USA.

programme.title: Fishing Impossible
programme.desc: Every autumn millions of salmon run up the rivers of British Columbia to spawn. But after months of drought the guys are forced to venture deep into the mountains to find the fish.

programme.title: China with Ben Fogle
programme.desc: Ben dives into China's history, culture and fast-paced modern life, from the ancient Great Wall to bustling Shanghai. 1/3.
